headline: CoU students block Dhaka-Chattogram highway demanding justice for Opratim
summary: Students of Comilla University protested the murder of Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, the son of a faculty member, demanding a speedy trial and execution of the killers.
details: Students of Comilla University (CoU) blocked the Dhaka-Chattogram highway at Kotbari Bishwa Road for nearly two hours today, demanding justice for the murder of Ishiat Shahriar Opratim.
Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor of the university's Department of Bangla.
The protest occurred after the students attended Opratim's first janaza on the university campus, accompanying the ambulance carrying his body.
The protesters issued a four-point ultimatum, demanding the arrest of all involved and the completion of the trial within 60 days, followed by the death sentence.
They also called for the withdrawal of the Cumilla SP and the OCs of Adarsha Sadar and Sadar South police stations, holding them accountable for the incident.

Additional demands included the establishment of a permanent police outpost near the university and nationwide measures to improve law and order, including an immediate-response unit for missing persons.
Police officials met with the protesters and stated that they have received the demands and will communicate them to higher authorities.
The blockade was withdrawn around 1:00 pm, restoring vehicular movement on the busy highway.
Police investigations revealed that the motive behind the killing was to steal an iPhone, and the phone has since been recovered from a suspect's house.
caption:
Students of Comilla University blocked the Dhaka-Chattogram highway for two hours, demanding justice for the murder of a faculty member's son.

Students of Comilla University (CoU) blocked the Dhaka-Chattogram highway at Kotbari Bishwa Road for nearly two hours today, demanding justice for the murder of Ishiat Shahriar Opratim.

Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor of the university's Department of Bangla.

The protest occurred after the students attended Opratim's first janaza on the university campus, accompanying the ambulance carrying his body.

The protesters issued a four-point ultimatum, demanding the arrest of all involved and the completion of the trial within 60 days, followed by the death sentence.

They also called for the withdrawal of the Cumilla SP and the OCs of Adarsha Sadar and Sadar South police stations, holding them accountable for the incident.

Additional demands included the establishment of a permanent police outpost near the university and nationwide measures to improve law and order, including an immediate-response unit for missing persons.

Police officials met with the protesters and stated that they have received the demands and will communicate them to higher authorities.

The blockade was withdrawn around 1:00 pm, restoring vehicular movement on the busy highway.

Police investigations revealed that the motive behind the killing was to steal an iPhone, and the phone has since been recovered from a suspect's house.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline: 4 arrested over cocktail explosions in Dhaka
summary: The Detective Branch of DMP arrested four people, including an Awami League leader, following crude bomb blasts outside Jatrabari Police Station.
details: The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested four people, including a unit Awami League leader, over cocktail explosions outside Jatrabari Police Station in Dhaka.
The arrestees are Md Rayhan Uddin, 35, Rasel Khan, 32, Ala Uddin, 28, and Abdullah, 28. Police recovered four unexploded cocktails from the suspects.
According to the DB, several cocktails exploded in front of the police station around 8:00 PM on September 18, injuring an autorickshaw driver.
Police identified the primary suspect, Rayhan, through CCTV footage. He was arrested during a drive in Bangshal, and subsequent raids in Lalbagh and Demra led to the arrest of the other three.
Rayhan is the office secretary of Unit 6 of Ward 32 under Bangshal Police Station of the Dhaka South unit of the Awami League. He had previously been jailed for five months in an anti-terrorism case.
Police claim all four suspects are active members of the Awami League, which is currently banned. They were allegedly carrying out the attacks to create public panic.
A case has been filed with Jatrabari Police Station, and police will seek remand for the four suspects to further investigate the involvement of others.
